response.markdown_report:
At 10% progress, retain **bounded title-confusable negative replacement** as an exploratory sampler experiment, with recent-terminal/Cloze training unchanged. Its incremental benefit and semantic mechanism remain unmeasured.

**Insights from the supplied evidence.** (1) Recent-terminal supervision addresses older-interest revival, but cannot identify fulfilled needs. (2) Broad matches outranking direct connections motivate finer discrimination; title overlap supplies imperfect clues, not verified compatibility. (3) Electronics has the weakest diagnostic separation: 6.62% negative-beats-positive and 0.7269 lower-tail margin. These training metrics do not establish validation ranking quality. The historical 0.5737 score does not identify component effects or establish a matched control.

**Insights from related work.** (1) BERT4Rec [1] supports retaining masked reconstruction and appended-mask inference. (2) S³-Rec [2] motivates attribute-sensitive supervision, without validating lexical negatives. (3) Sampled-softmax analysis [3] motivates competitive supervision; PSL [4], SRNS [6] and UFNRec [7] expose false-negative risks. (4) Hard-sampling theory [5] concerns model-score hardness; lexical similarity is a different property. Popularity evidence [8] suggests another possible confound.

| Direction | Existing mechanism | Proposed gap test |
|---|---|---|
| Current intent | Recent terminal targets | Retain recent context exposure |
| Specificity | Attribute-sensitive supervision | Test title-confusable candidates |
| Robustness | Uniform candidate competition | Cap replacement at 8/64 |
| Attribution | Score hardness and popularity | Measure confounds; defer additional controls |

Scores are Originality/Potential/User alignment/Model alignment/Difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each dimension includes positive (+) and negative (−) reasons.

| Idea | Scores | Critical assessment by dimension |
|---|---|---|
| **Title-confusable replacement** | **4/6/6/6/5** | O: + focused combination; − established mining. P: + cheap hypothesis; − uncertain mechanism. U: + recent/direct intent hypothesis; − suitability unknown. M: + targeted competition; − hardness unverified. D: + unchanged network; − exact sparse retrieval needs care. |
| Joint title-token auxiliary loss [2] | 5/7/7/6/6 | O: + adaptation; − established multitask learning. P: + transferable features; − sparse text. U: + distinguishing attributes; − topic shortcuts. M: + richer supervision; − loss conflict. D: + one network; − vocabulary/balancing work. |
| Bounded negative weighting [4] | 3/6/5/7/4 | O: + focused adaptation; − known objectives. P: + robustness; − uncertain transfer. U: + protects plausible matches; − weak specificity. M: + bounded influence; − weaker separation. D: + loss change; − calibration needed. |

**Selected algorithm.** Retain separately normalized 50:50 recent-terminal/Cloze losses. Replace eight of 64 uniform negatives with reproducibly sampled positive-similarity title neighbors, excluding complete training histories; uniformly fill shortages. Preserve identifiers and numbers. Target titles guide sampling only, never masked inputs or inference scores.

The complete recipe targets **older-interest revival** through retained terminal supervision and **broad-over-direct ranking** through lexical competition. Only the latter changes experimentally; neither behavioral improvement is established. Track uniform-negative diagnostic errors, lexical overlap, model scores and training frequencies.

Compare with a matched uniform control under fixed compute and sampled-candidate macro validation HR@10. Gains alone cannot establish semantic discrimination, full-catalog superiority [9], or reduced incompatibility. Report paired category differences and conditional bootstrap intervals when available; checkpoint selection creates optimism [10]. Deploy exactly one checkpoint per category.

References: numbered works and implementation references appear in `related_work`.

idea.description: Test replacing eight of 64 uniform training negatives with positive-similarity title-confusable candidates in each category's single corrected BERT4Rec. Retain separately normalized recent-terminal and ordinary Cloze objectives, and compare against an otherwise identical uniform-negative control. Treat lexical similarity, model-score hardness and popularity as distinct properties.
idea.motivation: Retained recent-terminal supervision addresses revival of older isolated interests. Lexical candidate competition tests whether the network can rank direct recent-interest connections above broad matches. These are two user-facing hypotheses for the complete recipe; the proposed comparison isolates only the incremental sampler change and cannot attribute improvements to recent-terminal supervision. Electronics' 6.62% diagnostic negative-beats-positive rate and 0.7269 lower-tail margin motivate a discrimination experiment, but neither demonstrates a semantic failure nor predicts validation gains. Titles cannot establish ownership, fulfilled needs, exact compatibility or current intent. Retain this small experiment at 10% progress rather than adding a text encoder, temporal architecture or additional sampling conditions before its feasibility and mechanism are assessed.
idea.implementation_notes:
This is an implementation specification for the supplied corrected baseline, whose source is absent from the prompt, rather than executable replacement files. Preserve its BERT4Rec architecture, optimizer, architecture hyperparameters and predictor writer. Resolve baseline-dependent numerical settings from the supplied baseline and record them before execution; do not invent missing settings. Use one independently trained model per category and one checkpoint per category at inference. Never combine experimental conditions, checkpoints or independently fitted predictors. Lexical scores are used exclusively for training-candidate selection and never added to neural recommendation scores.

Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl with existing routing. DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; all generated artifacts stay beneath the trial directory. Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per completed epoch. Preserve fixed splits and the host evaluator. Keep execution single-GPU. Do not inspect other trials, reuse their checkpoints, fetch extra datasets or pretrained weights, read hidden test files or alter evaluation.

Use the specified mixed objective in both conditions. For baseline batch size B>=2, use floor(B/2) terminal examples and the remainder corrected baseline Cloze examples. Sample users uniformly with replacement from training users having at least two interactions. For history length n, choose zero-based terminal target t uniformly from n-min(10,n-1) through n-1, inclusive. Construct history[max(0,t-(L-1)):t] followed by MASK and left-pad to L. Omit the complete future suffix. Retain corrected baseline Cloze windowing and target-selection rules for the other component; record their actual settings. Replace every supervised target with MASK, with no unchanged-target corruption. Ensure at least one supervised position per eligible Cloze example. Average losses over valid supervised positions separately within terminal and Cloze components, then combine with weights 0.5 each. If one component is empty, use the other with weight 1 and record the event; skip an update only when both are empty. This is a fixed mixture, not an epoch curriculum or per-example normalization.

Build a deterministic lexical index separately per category from titles associated with the already supplied catalog. Do not expand catalog membership or inspect held-out interactions. Normalize titles with Unicode NFC and map U+2010, U+2011, U+2012, U+2013, U+2014, U+2212 and U+FF0D to ASCII hyphen. Treat missing or nonstring titles as empty. Configure TfidfVectorizer(analyzer='word', token_pattern=r'(?u)\b\w+(?:-\w+)*\b', lowercase=True, strip_accents=None, stop_words=None, ngram_range=(1,2), min_df=1, max_df=1.0, max_features=None, binary=False, norm='l2', use_idf=True, smooth_idf=True, sublinear_tf=False, dtype=np.float64). The explicit (1,2) setting retains the original proposal's adjacent token bigrams in addition to individual tokens; it deliberately differs from the supplied search suggestion's unigram-only setting. Preserve numeric and single-character tokens and ASCII-hyphen identifiers such as WH-1000XM5. Tokenization preserves textual clues rather than establishing their meaning or compatibility.

Order catalog rows by ascending integer model item ID. Freeze and save title normalization rules, vocabulary, IDF, item-ID mapping, vectorizer configuration and package versions beneath the trial directory. TF-IDF fitting is candidate-selection preprocessing, not an independently trained recommendation predictor. If the entire category vocabulary is empty, record that condition and use uniform negatives throughout.

For each target item, retrieve at most 128 other catalog items with strictly positive TF-IDF cosine similarity, excluding PAD, MASK and the target. L2 normalization makes sparse dot products cosine similarities. Rank by descending computed similarity, breaking exact ties by ascending integer item ID. Use np.lexsort((item_ids, -scores)) when sorting retained candidates; do not use an arbitrary argpartition cutoff that discards preferred tied IDs. Apply global exclusions before selecting the 128 neighbors. Apply user-history exclusions later during sampling. Thus the operational pool is a filtered global top-128 list, not the top 128 eligible neighbors for each user; do not backfill from lower-ranked lexical neighbors after user exclusions. This truncation can increase uniform fallback and must be reported.

Compute exact neighbors using sparse query-by-catalog multiplication with query blocks of 128 rows and catalog blocks of 4096 rows, allowing smaller final blocks. After every product, discard excluded and nonpositive entries, retain each query's best 128 under the same total ordering, and merge with previously retained candidates. Never materialize a full catalog-by-catalog matrix. Record actual block settings and peak process memory where available: sparse products, library workspaces and inputs contribute memory beyond retained neighbors. Fixed blocks bound intermediate dimensions, not total memory. Preserve only positive-similarity neighbors: zero similarities, including empty-title rows, are deliberately excluded because arbitrary zero-overlap IDs would not implement the lexical hypothesis. Uniform fallback handles their absence. The search recommendation to include implicit zeros applies to a general exact top-k definition; this experiment explicitly defines a positive-similarity pool instead. ID tie-breaking resolves exact ties, not floating-point differences across environments.

For user u, eligible negatives are real catalog IDs excluding PAD, MASK and every item in u's complete training history, including all supervised positives. Never inspect validation or test labels for exclusions. Draw an ordered, uniform, unique base set of min(64, eligible_count) items. In the control, use this entire base set. In the proposal, when eligible_count>=64, retain its first 56 and sample up to eight items uniformly without replacement from the target's positive-similarity neighbor list after excluding the user's training history and retained 56. Fill remaining slots uniformly without replacement from the eligible catalog excluding retained and lexical items. The original final eight base items remain eligible for lexical selection or uniform refill; overlap with the original base set is allowed. The final set must contain 64 distinct items. If eligible_count<64, use every eligible item in both conditions. If it is zero, skip that target and record it. Use exact complement sampling or a bounded rejection procedure with exact-complement fallback, never unbounded rejection.

Use temperature-1 positive-plus-negative candidate cross-entropy, with unused batching slots masked to negative infinity. This is an uncorrected sampled candidate-classification objective. Lexical sampling changes its negative distribution; do not claim an unbiased approximation to full softmax or add an unspecified logQ correction. The always-present positive and sampled negatives play different roles. Gather supervised hidden states before scoring and use memory-safe microbatches. Compute full-batch valid terminal/Cloze denominators first, backpropagate each microbatch's weighted loss sum divided by its original component denominator, and step once per optimizer batch. Do not average unequal chunk means or split the candidate axis into independently normalized softmaxes. Keep microbatch settings identical across conditions and retain baseline gradient clipping when configured.

Use independent deterministic RNG streams for initialization, examples, Cloze masks, uniform base candidates, lexical choices, uniform refill, dropout and diagnostics. Derive non-dropout streams from numpy.random.SeedSequence([42, category_index, stream_index]) with category order fixed as listed above; record stream indices, RNG algorithms and states. Initialize each category model with seed 42 as required by the baseline. Do not include condition identity in shared example, masking or base-candidate stream seeds. Lexical selection and refill must not advance example, base-candidate or dropout streams. Use fixed-shape sampling or per-target keyed streams so skipped targets cannot desynchronize later paired base pools. Record any GPU nondeterminism rather than asserting bitwise identity. Initialize conditions independently from the same seed; do not load another trial's checkpoint.

Compare the proposal with a configuration-matched uniform control. The historical 0.5737 score alone does not establish a match, and the failed inspiration does not establish a measured result for this proposal. Keep architecture, optimizer, example construction, loss, initialization, batch and microbatch sizes, negative counts, and all unrelated settings identical. Title preprocessing should not affect either condition's model inputs or example sequence. Precompute lexical artifacts once for the proposal, without treating their absence from the control as a model change.

Before execution, record the remaining portion of the shared 43,200 GPU-second allowance and allocate half to each condition, equally across its four categories, including training, validation, diagnostics and failures. Reserve required diagnostic time using available host timing information rather than invented estimates. Record lexical preprocessing wall time and peak CPU memory separately and charge any GPU work to the shared allowance. Do not silently reallocate failed-run budgets or add tuning configurations. Stop training at completed epochs inside allocated caps, with a maximum of 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches in every completed epoch. Report updates, masked-target counts, runtime and stopping reasons because equal compute can yield unequal exposure.

Before training, record the actual checkpoint cadence supported by the unchanged host workflow; use that same cadence for both conditions. If the host supports only final evaluation, use the common completed endpoint rather than inventing intermediate access. A selection checkpoint is eligible only when all four category models in both conditions completed the same epoch on the predeclared evaluation grid. Select each condition's highest macro validation HR@10 on this shared grid, breaking epoch ties toward the earlier checkpoint; select the proposal only for a strictly higher best macro score, with condition ties favoring uniform. Deploy that condition's corresponding same-epoch four-category bundle. Do not independently choose category epochs, combine conditions or average checkpoints. If no common eligible checkpoint exists, report an incomplete comparison; do not manufacture a winner or expand the budget. Compute-limited endpoints outside the shared grid are descriptive only.

Use identical pinned validation users and candidate sets: 200 users/category, one positive and 99 unique negatives, evaluation seed 42. Describe results as sampled-candidate validation HR@10, not full-catalog HR@10. If the host supplies per-user hit indicators, report category differences and discordant hit counts. Bootstrap paired user records with replacement separately within each category, retaining 200 records/category, using seed 42 and 10,000 replicates. For each replicate, average paired differences within categories and then equally across four categories; report the observed macro difference and 2.5th/97.5th percentiles. These exploratory intervals condition on fitted models and fixed candidate sets, exclude training-seed and candidate-sampling variability, and do not correct checkpoint-selection optimism. Without hit indicators, report aggregate results without invented intervals. One changed hit changes category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. Record all tried configurations and selection opportunities, and freeze selection before the host's untouched held-out evaluation.

On fixed, training-only diagnostic examples, retain the original uniform-negative stream and original metric definitions so changing the optimization sampler does not mechanically redefine existing errors. Add separately named descriptive measurements: lexical replacement and fallback counts, positive title-overlap distributions, current-model negative-score distributions, positive-minus-negative margins, selected-item training-frequency distributions and eligible-pool sizes. Compute item frequencies exclusively from training interactions. Score both candidate types using the same checkpoint in evaluation mode without gradients and restore its previous mode afterward; never feed diagnostic results into sampling or selection. Record measured counts and unavailable values explicitly. Raw margins are scale-sensitive; title similarity is not score hardness, the embedding cosine statistic is not recommendation diversity, and one-negative training errors do not estimate host HR@10.

A gain over uniform could reflect score hardness, item frequency, memorization or lexical discrimination. The two-condition experiment cannot distinguish these explanations. Popularity-matched random and model-score-hard controls are sensible later comparisons, contingent on a new predeclared budget, and are not additional trials authorized by this proposal. Existing score-hardness results under BPR and popularity results under SASRec/BCE do not establish transfer to BERT4Rec candidate cross-entropy. Lexical neighbors can be plausible unseen positives; excluding known training positives does not remove that risk. The fixed eight-item cap limits exposure but has no demonstrated false-negative robustness guarantee. Do not relabel selected items as confirmed negatives, borrow robustness claims from PSL/SRNS/UFNRec, or tune neighbor counts and replacement fractions repeatedly on the same validation users.

Preserve ModelView, view.model as the actual trained nn.Module, item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data interfaces. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis) using measured values and their definitions. Diagnostic batches remain (None, sequence, positive, negative), each B x L, with valid family-specific MASK supervision. Only public histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps are available. Reviews, ratings, item categories, prices, stores, ownership, fulfilled needs and simulator traits remain unavailable; never infer their presence from generic data-schema examples.

Inference keeps at most L-1 history items, appends the reserved MASK, left-pads and gathers the final nonpadding position using explicit position indices, never count-1. Exclude PAD and MASK from outputs. Verify checkpoint configuration and embedded predictor consistency even though architecture is unchanged; working/predict.py must load exactly one selected neural checkpoint per category. No title-index artifact is required at inference. Retain full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for the twenty training simulator users, five/category, as qualitative diagnosis. Report those outcomes separately from sampled validation selection, and do not assert reduced compatibility failures, fulfilled-need repetition or full-catalog superiority without corresponding evidence.
idea.pseudocode:
Predeclare conditions uniform64 and title8; record remaining budget, supported checkpoint grid, tie rules and RNG streams.
Freeze baseline-dependent settings and all four category routes.
For each category:
    Normalize supplied catalog titles with the specified Unicode and dash rules.
    Fit the specified unigram-plus-bigram TF-IDF vectorizer; save vocabulary, IDF and item mapping.
    Compute exact positive-similarity top-128 neighbors using bounded query/catalog blocks.
    Exclude PAD, MASK and self before selection; sort by (-similarity, integer_item_id).
    Preserve only strictly positive similarities; record empty vocabulary/title cases.
For each condition and category:
    Initialize one corrected BERT4Rec independently with seed 42.
    For each completed epoch, run exactly 200 optimizer batches:
        Construct matched recent-terminal and corrected Cloze examples.
        Replace all supervised targets with MASK; omit terminal future suffixes.
        For each supervised target y belonging to user u:
            eligible = real_catalog minus set(full_training_history[u])
            base = shared_ordered_uniform_unique_sample(eligible, min(64, len(eligible)))
            if condition == title8 and len(eligible) >= 64:
                retained = base[:56]
                pool = positive_title_neighbors[y] intersect eligible minus set(retained)
                lexical = separate_stream_uniform_unique_sample(pool, min(8, len(pool)))
                fill_pool = eligible minus set(retained) minus set(lexical)
                fill = separate_stream_uniform_unique_sample(fill_pool, 8-len(lexical))
                negatives = retained + lexical + fill
            else:
                negatives = base
            Skip targets without negatives; record counts and fallbacks.
        Determine full-batch valid supervised counts for both components.
        Zero gradients once.
        For each fixed input microbatch:
            Encode masked sequences with gradients enabled.
            Score each positive and its complete candidate set through this BERT4Rec.
            Compute temperature-1 per-target candidate cross-entropy.
            Backpropagate component-weighted sums divided by full-batch component counts.
        Apply preserved clipping and update once when at least one component is valid.
        Charge GPU work to the condition/category allocation.
    Save trial-local checkpoints and invoke only host-supported unchanged validation.
Compare conditions on the predeclared epoch grid completed by all eight training runs.
Select by macro sampled-candidate HR@10; earlier-epoch ties win, condition ties favor uniform.
If no common eligible checkpoint exists, report the comparison as incomplete.
When host per-user hits exist, report paired category differences and stratified bootstrap intervals.
Label intervals exploratory and conditional; record all selection opportunities.
Deploy the winning same-epoch bundle: exactly one checkpoint per category.
Emit matching appended-MASK inference using explicit final nonpadding positions.
Run preserved uniform-negative diagnostics and separately labeled sampler-behavior measurements.
Do not combine lexical scores, conditions, checkpoints or independently trained predictors.

originality.positive: Combines title-sensitive candidate selection with explicitly recent terminal supervision in a small, falsifiable BERT4Rec experiment.
originality.negative: Lexical negative mining and recent-target sampling are established mechanisms; no controlled evidence establishes a new semantic discrimination principle.

future_potential.positive: A bounded experiment can establish feasibility and motivate later controlled comparisons or jointly trained text representations.
future_potential.negative: Any gain could arise from popularity or score hardness rather than semantic specificity, while plausible-positive contamination and benchmark dependence limit transfer.

code_difficulty.positive: The neural architecture, checkpoint format and inference scoring remain unchanged.
code_difficulty.negative: Exact sparse retrieval with deterministic ties, identifier-preserving tokenization, reproducible paired sampling, normalized microbatch losses and budget-compatible checkpoint selection require substantial care.

related_work.title: [1] BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Establishes bidirectional masked-item modeling for sequential recommendation.
Provides the backbone and appended-mask inference foundation retained here.
limitations: Does not establish the effectiveness of title-confusable negatives on this benchmark.
Masked reconstruction does not identify current need, ownership or exact compatibility.

related_work.title: [2] S³-Rec: Self-Supervised Learning for Sequential Recommendation with Mutual Information Maximization
contributions: Uses item–attribute and sequence–attribute relationships alongside masked-item learning.
Motivates studying distinguishing item information under sparse interaction supervision.
limitations: Its attribute objectives differ from lexical negative selection.
Its reported results do not establish gains under the supplied restrictions and evaluator.

related_work.title: [3] Sampled-softmax analysis (TOIS 2024; supplied reference)
contributions: Motivates multi-negative competition and implicit emphasis on higher-scoring negatives.
limitations: Does not establish an optimal lexical replacement fraction.
Nonuniform lexical selection changes the candidate objective; unbiased full-softmax estimation does not follow.

related_work.title: [4] PSL (2024 preprint; supplied reference)
contributions: Examines softmax sensitivity to false negatives and alternative activation-based ranking objectives.
limitations: Does not validate lexical candidates as true negatives.
Its robustness results do not automatically transfer to candidate cross-entropy with lexical sampling.

related_work.title: [5] On the Theories Behind Hard Negative Sampling
contributions: Connects score-based hard sampling under BPR to top-K ranking objectives.
Studies controllable model-score hardness.
limitations: Lexical similarity is not model-score hardness.
Results under BPR do not establish effectiveness for BERT4Rec sampled cross-entropy.

related_work.title: [6] SRNS: Simplify and Robustify Negative Sampling for Implicit Collaborative Filtering
contributions: Uses prediction scores and variance to address false-negative risks during sampling.
limitations: The proposed static lexical sampler does not implement prediction-variance filtering.
Its findings do not establish which title neighbors are genuine negatives.

related_work.title: [7] UFNRec (SDM 2023; supplied reference)
contributions: Studies identifying and exploiting likely false negatives in sequential recommendation.
limitations: Does not justify penalizing all unseen lexical neighbors.
Its false-negative treatment is not implemented by an eight-candidate replacement cap.

related_work.title: [8] Prakash et al. (2024), negative-sampling comparison supplied in the search results
contributions: Compares six samplers with SASRec/BCE across three datasets and twenty repeats.
Highlights accuracy and popularity-balance tradeoffs.
limitations: Uses a different backbone and objective.
Does not isolate popularity effects in title-based BERT4Rec negative sampling.

related_work.title: [9] On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled evaluation metrics can reverse recommender comparisons.
limitations: Does not authorize changing the pinned host benchmark.
Sampled-candidate gains still require separate evidence for full-catalog conclusions.

related_work.title: [10] On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains selection bias from optimizing model choices on finite validation data.
Motivates documenting search breadth and preserving untouched final evaluation.
limitations: A post-selection paired bootstrap does not remove adaptive selection optimism.
Does not supply benchmark-specific uncertainty estimates.

related_work.title: Scikit-learn TfidfVectorizer documentation
contributions: Documents explicit tokenization, n-gram, normalization and IDF settings needed for reproducible lexical indexing.
limitations: Default tokenization does not preserve hyphenated identifiers as required here.
Token preservation does not establish semantic equivalence or compatibility.

related_work.title: SciPy sparse CSR dot documentation
contributions: Provides sparse matrix multiplication for blocked TF-IDF similarity computation.
limitations: Sparse products can contain dense blocks and substantial temporary workspace.
Does not implement the proposal's exclusion, positive-similarity filtering or deterministic top-k policy.

related_work.title: Scikit-learn pairwise_distances_chunked documentation
contributions: Documents chunked pairwise computation and its working-memory setting.
limitations: Working-memory settings do not bound total process memory.
The proposed exact retrieval explicitly bounds both query and catalog block dimensions.

related_work.title: NumPy lexsort documentation
contributions: Supports ordering by descending similarity with ascending item-ID tie-breaking.
limitations: Resolves exact ties, not floating-point differences across environments.
Cannot repair preferred tied candidates already discarded by an arbitrary partition cutoff.

related_work.title: NumPy argpartition documentation
contributions: Documents partition-based selection useful when boundary ties are handled explicitly.
limitations: Does not guarantee the desired item-ID ordering among tied cutoff candidates.
The proposed implementation uses a total ordering during every block merge.

related_work.title: SciPy bootstrap documentation
contributions: Documents bootstrap resampling and paired-data options.
limitations: Category-stratified macro differences require preserving category structure explicitly.
Resampling fixed evaluation outcomes excludes training variability and does not correct model-selection bias.

related_work.title: Correcting the LogQ Correction (RecSys 2025; supplied reference)
contributions: Distinguishes the always-present positive from sampled negatives when analyzing sampling corrections.
limitations: Sampling correction addresses a different issue from false-negative robustness.
No correction is implemented or unbiased full-softmax claim made in this proposal.
